rationale: Psalm 107:23-30 narrates the same sequence of events Matthew 8:23-27 narrates: people at sea, a storm that lifts "the waves of the sea" (107:25, BSB), a cry for help in distress (107:28), and a calm that only God brings: "He calmed the storm to a whisper, and the waves of the sea were hushed" (107:29, BSB). In Matthew, Jesus himself rebukes "the winds and the sea, and it was perfectly calm" (8:26, BSB). Matthew gives no citation formula and no shared wording beyond the ordinary vocabulary of a storm at sea, so this is graded as an allusion, not a quotation. It is graded plausible rather than strong because the one named reader found making the link is John Chrysostom, as excerpted in the Catena Aurea. He applies the Psalm ("He spake, and the storm of wind ceases", bracketed there as Ps 107:25) to Christ, who "fulfilled in deed" what was said of the Father. No modern commentary making the link was read for this lesson, and the Greek of Matthew was not compared with the Septuagint of this Psalm.
